key_semantic_findings: SAIL-VOS is the strongest accessible synthetic amodal video label reference: explicit paired modal and per-object amodal masks with stable IDs.

TAO-Amodal has amodal bounding boxes and visibility, including fully invisible and out-of-frame, but no amodal masks; it is the closest real-video evaluation reference for separating hidden from out-of-view geometry at box level.
OVIS and MOSE have real modal masks with occlusion/challenge context, but neither verifiedly supplies pixel-level full-occlusion amodal truth or physical-occluder labels.
TAP-Vid and PointOdyssey support point visibility/correspondence, not instance-level amodal segmentation or individual identity recovery.
resource_relationships: MOVi-A--F are Kubric challenge resources (official path: github.com/google-research/kubric/tree/main/challenges/movi), not an independent paper record: their arXiv identifier is Kubric's 2203.03570 and is deliberately retained only as a resource relationship to avoid duplicate-paper merging.
access_and_license_risks: SAIL-VOS requires GTA V ownership and restricts use to non-commercial research/education with no redistribution.
TAO-Amodal has gated AVA/HACS videos and no-redistribution/non-commercial terms despite repository metadata.
TABE code is MIT, but third-party models, checkpoints and dataset download terms are separate.
unresolved: No primary Zenodo/HAL/OpenAIRE/CORE record was retained: searches produced generic or unrelated results rather than a verified source matching these six facets.

Amodal SAM (arXiv:2604.20748) is confirmed by the parent as a 2026 paper, but exact AmodalSAM2 is not established; its official code/repository should be verified in a scholarly/official-code bucket before merge.
TABE-51’s label-production details and whether every fully hidden target represents a real physical occlusion rather than its generation protocol require full-paper review.
